title: Preview the built site
text:
Description
Serves docs/ (or docs/dev/, for a development site; see the Configuration section of build_site()), as built by build_site(), in a web browser. The server keeps running for the rest of the R session and is reused by later calls, including build_site()’s (which, with a server already running, leaves the open page to reload instead of opening another). It keeps serving the previous site while build_site() runs. An open page reloads if the new build changed it.

The site’s local URL, invisibly.

build_site()
preview_site()

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text: Source: R/use_quartodown_action.R

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Description
Writes .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml, a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site and deploys it to the gh-pages branch. It runs build_site() on every push, pull request and release, but only deploys when it isn’t a pull request. Also adds ^\.github$ to .Rbuildignore if it’s not already there.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Usage
use_quartodown_action(path = ".", overwrite = FALSE)

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.




overwrite


Logical. Replace an existing .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml? By default it’s left as is.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Details
Once the workflow’s first run has created the gh-pages branch, go to the Pages section of the repository’s settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to the workflow file.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown_action(pkg)
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmpSf0ROq/examplepkg19bc213a5e10/.github/workflows/quartodown.yaml.
#> ✔ Added `^\.github$` to /tmp/RtmpSf0ROq/examplepkg19bc213a5e10/.Rbuildignore.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#> 1. Commit and push the workflow.
#> 2. Once its first run has created the `gh-pages` branch, go to the Pages
#> section of the repository's settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that
#> branch.
list.files(pkg, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
#> [1] ".github/workflows/quartodown.yaml" ".Rbuildignore"                    
#> [3] "DESCRIPTION"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Technical details
text:
Source: vignettes/articles/technical.qmd
quartodown generates a Quarto website project from the package sources, so the man pages, vignettes and generated pages are all Quarto pages, and every Quarto feature works.

title: Technical details
text:
How a build works
quartodown::build_site() runs in three stages:

Before rendering, it installs the package into a temporary library, writes a Quarto project into _quarto/ and runs the reference pages’ examples against that package.
During rendering, Quarto renders _quarto/ into _quarto/_site/, running the vignettes against that package.
After rendering, it links code to its documentation, adds hover tooltips, puts the logo by each page’s title and writes the redirect pages. Finally, the finished site replaces the one in docs/.

Until that last step, docs/ still has the previous site, also if the build fails.
With development: mode: devel, the site goes in docs/dev/ instead, and a build into docs/ leaves dev/ as it is.
In an interactive session it then serves the site with preview_site(). The server keeps running for the rest of the session, so you can keep reading the previous site during a rebuild, and after it an open page that changed reloads instead of a new one opening.
build_site(devel = TRUE) skips the install and loads the package from source with pkgload::load_all() instead. It is faster, but code that starts other R processes (for example with callr or parallel) won’t find the package, and build-stage \Sexpr{} macros in the man pages don’t run.
build_site()’s workers argument sets the number of processes to build with. More than one needs the mirai package.
build_site(freeze = TRUE) reuses the results of code from an earlier build, kept in _quarto/_freeze/, for pages whose source hasn’t changed (Quarto’s freeze). Committing _quarto/_freeze/ lets builds on CI reuse them too.






Warning



Freeze only checks each page’s own source, not your package’s code or the packages it uses. After changing a function or updating a dependency, the pages running that code keep their old output until you delete _quarto/_freeze/.


Throughout the build, the environment variable IN_QUARTODOWN is "true", so the package’s code can tell it is running for the site, and IN_QUARTODOWN_PKG is the package’s name.
_quarto/ is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by quartodown::use_quartodown(). To change the site, edit _quartodown/ instead (see Customizing your site).
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.qmd                     # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, titled, with issues and users linked
├── _quartodown/                  # the package's _quartodown/, as it is
└── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML

title: Technical details
text:
The man pages
Examples run, with their output in the same block as the code, prefixed with #>. To save Quarto starting an R process per page, they all run beforehand in one R process, which resets the global environment, search path, options and the like between pages, as R CMD check does. Pages whose examples fail or produce HTML widgets are left for Quarto to run.

title: Technical details
text:
Code links and tooltips
Function calls in R code, and inline code like mean() or ?mean, link to their documentation: the package’s own pages, another installed package’s site, or else rdrr.io. A package that isn’t installed, as in library(pkg), links to its site from its DESCRIPTION on CRAN, or else its repository or its CRAN page, but its functions aren’t linked. Where other packages’ sites are is cached in tools::R_user_dir("quartodown", "cache"), and looked up again when more than a week old; delete the folder to look them all up again.
The build also writes docs/pkgdown.yml, so that other packages’ sites, made with quartodown or pkgdown, can link to your pages.
References to the package’s own functions also get a hover tooltip with their usage and title. A usage longer than 12 lines is shortened. To build without tooltips, use build_site(tooltips = FALSE).

title: Technical details
text:
The theme
The site has a light and a dark theme, and follows the browser’s preference. Each is built in layers:

the Quarto theme: default in light mode and default with quartodown-dark.scss, its colors for a dark page, in dark mode, unless theme: picks others,
quartodown.scss, quartodown’s own styling,
_quartodown/extra.scss, if the package has one.

With the default light theme, quartodown-fonts.scss also gives the dark theme the same system fonts and heading sizes.
Code output keeps the colors packages such as cli give it in a terminal, in shades that suit the light or dark theme.

text: Source: R/use_quartodown.R

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Description
Writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, the configuration file build_site() reads. It starts with a reference: field listing every function currently documented in <path>/man/*.Rd in one "All functions" section. Also adds the .gitignore/.Rbuildignore entries the build needs (see Details) if they’re not already there.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Usage
use_quartodown(path = ".")

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Details
In a package with a pkgdown configuration (_pkgdown.yml, also in pkgdown/), it’s translated instead, with any files it needs, such as _quartodown/extra.scss, and the settings that couldn’t be translated are listed. See "Coming from pkgdown" in vignette("customizing", package = "quartodown").
An existing _quartodown.yml, or file in _quartodown/, is never overwritten.
use_quartodown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/

# .Rbuildignore
^docs$
^_quarto$
^_quartodown$


_quarto/ is the Quarto project build_site() generates and renders into docs/. Its _freeze/ directory holds the results of code run with build_site(freeze = TRUE), which can be committed so later builds, e.g. on CI, reuse them (they aren’t rerun when only the package’s code or its dependencies change, so delete it to refresh them). _quartodown/ holds the site’s configuration and any files it uses, such as extra.scss.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to _quartodown/_quartodown.yml.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown(pkg)
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmpjxdThV/examplepkg19c21b9f1069/_quartodown/_quartodown.yml (edit this to group your functions).
#> ✔ Added `_quarto/*` and `!_quarto/_freeze/` to /tmp/RtmpjxdThV/examplepkg19c21b9f1069/.gitignore.
#> ✔ Added `^docs$`, `^_quarto$`, and `^_quartodown$` to /tmp/RtmpjxdThV/examplepkg19c21b9f1069/.Rbuildignore.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#> 1. Edit _quartodown/_quartodown.yml to group your functions the way you want.
#> 2. Build and preview the site with `quartodown::build_site()`.
readLines(file.path(pkg, "_quartodown", "_quartodown.yml"))
#> [1] "# Configuration for quartodown::build_site(). See"                    
#> [2] "# vignette(\"customizing\", package = \"quartodown\") for all fields."
#> [3] ""                                                                     
#> [4] "reference:"                                                           
#> [5] "  - title: All functions"                                             
#> [6] "    contents:"                                                        
#> [7] "      []"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Changelog
text: Source: NEWS.md

title: Changelog
text:
quartodown (development version)

Code is now linked by quartodown itself instead of downlit, so code blocks keep Quarto’s highlighting, linking is more consistent, and builds work offline.
The default dark theme is now a dark version of Quarto’s default theme, with a neutral near-black page and soft blue links, rather than darkly. Use theme: dark: darkly to keep the old look.
build_site() builds the site in _quarto/_site/, and replaces the one in docs/ only when it’s complete. So the previous site stays in place during a build, and after a failed one. preview_site() now serves it with nanonext rather than servr, so it keeps working while build_site() runs. An open page reloads if the new build changed it.
use_quartodown() translates an existing _pkgdown.yml: the navbar and articles: become navbar: items and menus, template settings become theme:, quarto: settings and files in _quartodown/, and redirects keep pkgdown’s addresses of the vignettes and changelog working. It lists what it couldn’t translate.
New internal-pages: true setting, to build a page for every internal topic, not only those the reference index lists. Links to an internal topic without a page, from another topic’s documentation or the navbar, now warn.
The reference index shows lifecycle badges, and reference: takes pkgdown’s has_lifecycle() selector. A section titled internal is hidden, as in pkgdown.
New development: mode: setting in _quartodown.yml, as in pkgdown: with devel (or auto and a .9000 version), the site for the development version is built into docs/dev/, next to the released version’s. A switch next to the navbar’s title goes between them. auto keeps a package that isn’t on CRAN yet in docs/, as unreleased. Content marked .quartodown-devel or .quartodown-release is shown on only that site.
New workers argument to build_site(), to build the site with several processes. use_quartodown_action()’s workflow uses 4.
The reference pages’ examples now run before rendering, all in one R process, rather than Quarto starting one for each page, which made most of the build’s time for packages with many examples.
The package’s logo, man/figures/logo.svg or .png (.svg if both exist), now shows right of the title of every page, not just the home page, with logo-light.svg or .png in light mode if it exists. logo: false in _quartodown.yml turns it off.
build_site() reports its progress in a few steps (installing the package, writing the Quarto project, rendering, linking code), each with the time it took, and where it built the site. When a page fails to render with quiet = TRUE, Quarto’s error is now shown rather than a suggestion to rerun with quiet = FALSE.
The changelog page is now titled “Changelog”, with its versions’ headings a level down, and links its source, NEWS.md.
The search box’s magnifying glass and clear button are now readable in dark mode.

title: Changelog
text:
quartodown 0.1.0

Initial release.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Source: vignettes/customizing.qmd
If you want to customize your site, you can do so by editing _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, which quartodown::use_quartodown() creates. The _quartodown/ folder at the package root also holds the files that style the site. _quartodown.yml has nine fields, all optional:

title: Customizing your site
text:
The reference index
Without reference:, the index lists every function in one section. To group them, list the sections:
reference:
1  - title: Read and write
2    desc: Functions for getting data in and out.
    contents:
3      - read_data
4      - starts_with("write_")
  - title: Helpers
5    subtitle: Low-level
    contents:
      - has_concept("helpers")
6      - -internal_helper

1

Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.

2

Optional Markdown text, shown under the heading.

3

A topic, by any of its \alias{} names or its Rd file name.

4

A selector.

5

An optional heading one level below title.

6

A leading - removes a topic.


The selectors are:







Selector
Selects topics




starts_with("x"), ends_with("x"), contains("x")
with an alias that starts with, ends with or contains x


matches("regex")
with an alias matching a regular expression


has_concept("x"), has_keyword("x")
with that \concept{} or \keyword{}


has_lifecycle("x")
with that lifecycle badge, such as "deprecated"


c(...)
selected by any of the selectors given


- before a topic or selector
removed from those the entries above select, or as the first entry, from all topics



Topics that no section lists get a warning and are left off the index. The exception is \keyword{internal} topics, which are left out, without a page, unless named, as with roxygen’s reexports, or selected with internal = TRUE, as in starts_with("dev_", internal = TRUE).
Links to an internal topic without a page, from another topic’s documentation (\link{helper}, roxygen’s [helper()]) or from the navbar, get a warning. To build a page for every internal topic, set:
internal-pages: true
To leave a topic off the index without the warning, list it in a section titled internal, which isn’t shown.
The format is the same as pkgdown’s reference: field, so an existing one can be copied over.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The navbar
navbar: lists the items on the navbar’s left and right, in order, and under tools the icons right of the search box. The default is:
navbar:
  left: [intro, reference, articles, news]
  right: []
  tools: [repo]
Each of these is a keyword that quartodown turns into an item, and leaves out if the package has nothing for it:



Keyword
Item




intro
“Get started”: the vignette named after the package, or the only top-level vignette if there’s just one


reference
“Reference”: the function reference index


articles
“Articles”: a menu of every vignette no other item links, top-level ones first, then those in subfolders


news
“Changelog”: NEWS.md


repo
The repository, with a GitHub or GitLab icon (else a generic one)



Any other item is a vignette, given as its path relative to vignettes/ without extension and linked with its title, or a Quarto navbar item. tools takes only icons: repo or a Quarto tool. Inside a Quarto item’s menu:, vignettes are given the same way, and a folder ending in / lists every vignette in it.
For example, with the vignettes in a folder for each menu:
navbar:
  left:
    - reference
    - news
    - text: Get started
      menu:
1        - get-started/installation
        - get-started/first-steps
    - text: User guide
2      menu: user-guide/
    - text: Developers
      menu:
        - dev/internals
3        - text: Contributing
          href: CONTRIBUTING.md
  right:
    - text: Blog
      href: https://example.com/blog
  tools:
    - repo
    - icon: mastodon
      text: Mastodon
      href: https://fosstodon.org/@me

1

vignettes/get-started/installation.qmd.

2

Every vignette in vignettes/user-guide/, sorted by file name.

3

Any Quarto navbar item works in a menu too.


Vignettes can live in any subfolder of vignettes/. Files and folders whose name starts with _ or . are skipped, as Quarto does.
Every vignette is built, even one the navbar doesn’t link to. Such a vignette can only be reached through links from other pages, so build_site() warns about it, unless the navbar has articles, which lists every vignette nothing else links.






Note



R only builds top-level vignettes into the package, so vignettes in subfolders are website-only.



A sidebar instead
With style: sidebar, the left items move into a sidebar beside every page, and the navbar keeps the site’s title, the search box, the right items and the tools:
navbar:
  style: sidebar
Menus become sections of the sidebar, and “Reference” lists every reference page by function name, with a section for each titled group of reference:. The gallery shows what it looks like.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The home page
The home page shows README.md, or, if there is none, the package’s description from DESCRIPTION. To give the site a different home page than the README, use home: file: at another file, relative to the package root:
home:
  file: index.qmd
It can be Markdown (.md) or a Quarto document (.qmd), whose code runs when the site is built, as in a vignette. Write links and image paths in it relative to the package root, as in the README.
Next to the page, a sidebar shows the package’s links, license, community files, citation, authors and badges. sidebar: can reorder its sections, drop some, or add your own, and links: adds to its links:
home:
  links:
    - text: Blog
      href: https://example.com/blog
  sidebar:
1    structure: [links, funding, license, authors]
    components:
2      funding:
        title: Funding
        text: Supported by [a grant](https://example.com).

1

The sections, in order. The built-in ones are links, license, community, citation, authors and dev (the README’s badges); by default, all of them in that order, then your own.

2

A section of your own: a heading and Markdown text.


For full control over the page you can turn the sidebar off with sidebar: false:
home:
  file: index.qmd
  sidebar: false
The page then shows the file as written. Like any other page, it then gets a table of contents, which toc: false in its front matter can turn off.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Authors
The home page’s sidebar and the footer list the authors with the roles aut, cre and fnd from DESCRIPTION’s Authors@R, and the authors page lists everyone. authors: can link a person’s name, or replace it with HTML such as a logo, and change who is shown:
authors:
1  Jane Doe:
    href: https://jane.example.com
  Acme Inc:
    href: https://acme.example.com
    html: <img src="https://acme.example.com/logo.png" alt="Acme" height="24">
  sidebar:
2    roles: [aut, cre]
3    after: Thanks to all [contributors](authors.html).
  footer:
    roles: [cre]
4    text: Maintained by

1

A person, by their name as in Authors@R.

2

The roles shown in the sidebar.

3

Markdown shown under the sidebar’s list, or with before: above it.

4

Instead of “Developed by”.


The format is the same as pkgdown’s authors:.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The repository
Links to the package’s source code, issues and contributors come from the first GitHub, GitLab (also self-hosted, if the host name contains gitlab) or Codeberg URL in DESCRIPTION’s URL, or else from its BugReports. For a package in a subfolder, give the folder’s URL, such as https://github.com/me/repo/tree/main/mypkg.
repo: changes the branch the source links point to:
repo:
  branch: devel
or sets the links directly, such as for another host:
repo:
  url:
1    home: https://git.sr.ht/~me/mypkg
2    source: https://git.sr.ht/~me/mypkg/tree/main/item/
3    issue: https://todo.sr.ht/~me/mypkg/
4    user: https://sr.ht/~

1

The repository’s page.

2

Prefix of links to files, such as R/foo.R. Overrides branch:.

3

Prefix of links to issues.

4

Prefix of links to users.


The format is the same as pkgdown’s repo:.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Redirects
When a page moves, such as a function’s reference page after it is renamed you can use redirects: so links to the old address keeps working. Each entry is a pair: the old address and the new one, both relative to the site’s root:
redirects:
  - ["reference/foo.bar.html", "reference/foo_bar.html"]
  - ["articles/old-guide.html", "vignettes/guide.html"]
For a vignette, Quarto’s own aliases: in its front matter does the same.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Development and release sites
By default, every build replaces the site. To keep the site for the version on CRAN and have a second one, at dev/, for the development version, with a switch next to the navbar’s title to go between them, set development: mode::
development:
  mode: auto
Remember to bump the version to .9000 right after each release to avoid the release version of docs to be overwritten!






NoteAll modes





The modes are the same as pkgdown’s:

release (the default): builds into docs/.
devel: builds into docs/dev/ and marks the version as in development.
unreleased: builds into docs/ and marks the version as unreleased, for a package not yet on CRAN.
auto: devel for a version like 1.2.0.9000, or unreleased if the package isn’t on CRAN yet; otherwise release.

The environment variable QUARTODOWN_DEV_MODE overrides it.



Content for only one of the two sites can be set in a .quartodown-release or .quartodown-devel div or span:
::: {.quartodown-release}
Install the released version from CRAN with `install.packages("mypkg")`.
:::

::: {.quartodown-devel}
Install the development version with `pak::pak("me/mypkg")`.
:::
With mode: auto, a package not yet on CRAN keeps the .quartodown-devel content.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Files the vignettes use
The vignettes are built from a copy of vignettes/ in _quarto/vignettes/, so a relative path out of it, such as read.csv("../data-raw/example.csv"), can’t find the file. List such files and folders under vignettes: files:, and they are copied too, to the same paths:
vignettes:
  files:
    - data-raw/example.csv
Documents in them aren’t rendered as pages. When a vignette has a quoted ../ path to a file that isn’t copied, the build warns and names the entry to add.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Other Quarto settings
quartodown writes a Quarto configuration into _quarto/_quarto.yml (overwritten on every build). The quarto: field is merged over it, key by key:

A list of entries, such as website: navbar: left:, is added to.
Any other value is replaced.
~ removes a setting.

For example, to fold code blocks, drop the table of contents and change the footer:
quarto:
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
      toc: ~
  website:
    page-footer:
      right: "Built with love."
See the Quarto website reference for the full list of changes you can make.
quarto: applies to every page. To change a single vignette instead, set the option in its front matter, which overrides the site-wide value:
---
title: "A long tutorial"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    toc-depth: 3
---
To change a single code chunk, use a chunk option such as #| code-fold: true.

title: Customizing your site
Customizing your site
text:
Coming from pkgdown
In a package with a _pkgdown.yml, use_quartodown() translates it into _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, and lists the settings it couldn’t translate. Fields of the same format are copied: url:, reference:, home: sidebar:, home: links:, authors:, repo:, redirects: and development: mode:. The rest maps as follows:



pkgdown
quartodown




navbar:
navbar:, with links to quartodown’s pages


articles:
an “Articles” navbar menu, a section each


title:
quarto: website: navbar: title:


home: description:
quarto: website: description:


lang:
quarto: lang:


template: bootswatch:
theme: light:


template: bslib:
Sass variables in _quartodown/extra.scss


pkgdown/extra.scss, extra.css
_quartodown/extra.scss, extra.css


template: opengraph:
quarto: website: open-graph: and twitter-card:


template: includes:
files in _quartodown/, set as quarto: format: html: include-in-header: etc.


template: math-rendering:
quarto: format: html: html-math-method:


template: params: ganalytics:
quarto: website: google-analytics:


template: light-switch:
always on: the site has a light and a dark theme


toc: depth:
quarto: format: html: toc-depth:


figures:
quarto: format: html: fig-width:, fig-height:, fig-dpi:


footer:
not translated: authors: footer:, or quarto: website: page-footer:



Vignettes are published under vignettes/ rather than articles/, and the changelog is NEWS.html rather than news/index.html, so the translation adds redirects: from pkgdown’s addresses.
A separate home page (an index.md used instead of the README) isn’t picked up automatically: set it with home: file:. Code that checks IN_PKGDOWN (or pkgdown::in_pkgdown()) should check identical(Sys.getenv("IN_QUARTODOWN"), "true") instead.

title: quartodown
text:
quartodown is an R package that turns your package’s README, help pages and vignettes into a website, rendered entirely by Quarto.


Every page, help pages included, is a Quarto page, so you get:

every Quarto feature, from callouts and tabsets to code annotations and cross-references, on every page;
Quarto’s themes, extensions and settings.

On top of that, quartodown adds:

the package website layout R users know from pkgdown: a home page sidebar, a grouped function reference, articles and a changelog;
function links with hover tooltips.




Install the stable version from CRAN:
install.packages("quartodown")
or the development version from GitHub:
pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/quartodown")
quartodown also needs Quarto installed.



Browse the site to see how it looks! Quarto features shows callouts, tabsets, footnotes and more on a quartodown site. If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
If your package already has a pkgdown site, most of _pkgdown.yml can be copied over as is; see Coming from pkgdown.
Then build the site:
quartodown::build_site()
In an interactive session, this also opens the site in your browser.
To publish it on GitHub Pages, run quartodown::use_quartodown_action(). It writes a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site on every push and deploys it to the gh-pages branch.
See Customizing for everything _quartodown.yml can configure.

Using quartodown for your package? Feel free to open a pull request adding it to this list.

title: Build the package website
text:
Description
Builds the package website into docs/ with Quarto.

title: Build the package website
text:
Usage
build_site(
  path = ".",
  tooltips = TRUE,
  freeze = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE,
  devel = FALSE,
  workers = 1,
  preview = interactive()
)

title: Build the package website
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Give references to the package’s own functions (in code blocks and inline code) a hover tooltip showing the function’s usage and title?




freeze


Logical. Reuse the results of code that ran in an earlier build, for pages whose source hasn’t changed since? Uses Quarto’s freeze, which keeps them in _quarto/_freeze/. Changes to the package’s code or its dependencies aren’t detected; delete _quarto/_freeze/ to rerun everything.




quiet


Logical. Hide Quarto’s rendering output? If a page fails to render, its error is shown either way.




devel


Logical. By default, the examples and vignettes run against the package installed from path into a temporary library. With devel = TRUE, they run against it loaded with pkgload::load_all() instead, which is faster, but code that starts other R processes (e.g. with callr or parallel workers) won’t find the package there.




workers


Number of processes to build the site with. More than 1 needs the mirai package.




preview


Logical. Open the built site in a web browser with preview_site()? By default, only in interactive sessions.

title: Build the package website
text:
Details
The site is built in a scratch folder, _quarto/_site/, and replaces the one in docs/ only once it is complete. So the previous site stays there, and viewable with preview_site(), while the build runs and if it fails.
build_site() assembles a Quarto website project in _quarto/ from the package sources and _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, then renders it. It uses README.md (or, without one, DESCRIPTION), man/, the vignettes (including those in subfolders), NEWS.md, LICENSE/LICENSE.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and SUPPORT.md (at the top level or in .github/). See vignette("quartodown") for what the site contains.
While it builds, the environment variable IN_QUARTODOWN is "true", so the package’s examples and vignettes can check identical(Sys.getenv("IN_QUARTODOWN"), "true"). IN_QUARTODOWN_PKG is the name of the package whose site it is, which code shared between packages can check.

title: Build the package website
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to the built site.

title: Build the package website
text:
Configuration
_quartodown/_quartodown.yml is optional; use_quartodown() creates one. It can contain:


url: the site’s address. It defaults to the first URL in DESCRIPTION that isn’t a source repository.


reference: the sections of the function reference index and the topics each lists, by name or with selectors such as starts_with(). The format is the same as pkgdown’s.


navbar: the items on the navbar’s left and right: keywords such as reference and articles, vignettes, and Quarto navbar items and menus; and the icons in its tools, by default repo. With style: sidebar, the left items go in a sidebar instead, with a link to every reference page.


home: file, the .md or .qmd file the home page shows instead of README.md; sidebar, the sidebar’s structure (its sections, in order) and components (sections of your own), or false to show the page as written, without it; and links, added to the sidebar’s links.


authors: by a person’s name, an href to link it and html to replace it; and under sidebar and footer, the roles shown, with before/after text in the sidebar and text in the footer.


repo: the repository’s urls (home, and the prefixes of links to a file, source; an issue, issue; and a user, user) and branch. They default to those of DESCRIPTION’s GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg URL.


theme: the light and dark themes: names of Quarto’s built-in themes, such as flatly and darkly, or .scss files in _quartodown/. By default, default and a dark version of it.


redirects: pairs of paths, from an old page to the one replacing it, such as ["reference/old.html", "reference/new.html"].


development: mode, release (the default) to build the site into docs/, or devel to build a site for the development version into docs/dev/, next to the released version’s; unreleased marks the version as unreleased, and auto picks from the version number and whether the package is on CRAN. The environment variable QUARTODOWN_DEV_MODE overrides it. The format is the same as pkgdown’s. Content in .quartodown-devel or .quartodown-release shows on only that site.


vignettes: files, files and folders outside vignettes/ that the vignettes use by a relative path, such as man/rmd/ for a child document ../man/rmd/shared.Rmd, copied with them.


logo: false to leave the logo, man/figures/logo.svg or .png (and in light mode logo-light, if it exists), off the pages’ titles.


internal-pages: true to give every \keyword{internal} topic a reference page, rather than only those the reference index lists.


quarto: settings merged over the generated Quarto configuration.


_quartodown/extra.scss and _quartodown/extra.css, if they exist, style every page, on top of quartodown’s theme. The whole _quartodown/ folder is copied into the Quarto project, so quarto settings can refer to other files in it by the same path.
See vignette("customizing", package = "quartodown") for the details.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Source: vignettes/quartodown.qmd
quartodown builds a website for an R package with Quarto. This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Set up
From the root of your package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, and adds the files the build generates to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore. _quartodown.yml is where you can customize your site. If your package already has a _pkgdown.yml, see Coming from pkgdown for how its settings carry over.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Build the site
quartodown::build_site()
build_site() builds the site into docs/ and, in an interactive session, opens it in your browser. You can keep reading it during a rebuild, after which the page reloads if it changed, and preview_site() opens it again if you’ve closed it. Examples and vignettes run against your package’s current source. While iterating, build_site(devel = TRUE) is faster because it loads the package with pkgload::load_all() instead of installing it.
The following is added to your site:

Home page: your README.md. Next to it, a sidebar links to the source code, the bug tracker and CRAN (if the package is there), and shows the license, citation and authors from DESCRIPTION. Any badges in your README (between <!-- badges: start --> and <!-- badges: end -->) are moved into the sidebar.
Reference: a page for each help topic in man/, plus an index page listing them all.
Get started: the vignette with the same name as your package, like this one.
Articles: all your other vignettes, including any in subfolders such as vignettes/articles/.
Changelog: your NEWS.md. Issue numbers like #123 and GitHub usernames like @user become links.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Publish on GitHub Pages
To build the site and deploy it to the gh-pages branch on every push, add a GitHub Actions workflow:
quartodown::use_quartodown_action()
This writes .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml. Commit and push it. Once its first run has created the gh-pages branch, go to the Pages section of your repository’s settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Learn more
Customizing your site covers everything _quartodown.yml can change.
Gallery shows this site built with different settings, and the configuration behind each look.
Quarto features shows Quarto’s authoring features, such as callouts, tabsets and footnotes, on a quartodown site.
Technical details explains how a build works.

title: Quarto features
text:
Source: vignettes/articles/showcase.qmd
quartodown renders every page with Quarto itself, so all of Quarto’s features for writing documents work in your vignettes and articles. This page shows some of them as they look on a quartodown site, each with the source that makes it.

title: Quarto features
text:
Callouts






Note



Callouts draw attention to a piece of text. There are five types: note, tip, important, warning and caution.








TipTip with a title



Give a callout a title with a heading as its first line.








WarningClick to expand





Callouts can be collapsible, which is handy for details most readers can skip.





Source

::: {.callout-note}
Callouts draw attention to a piece of text. There are five types: `note`, `tip`,
`important`, `warning` and `caution`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip with a title

Give a callout a title with a heading as its first line.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Click to expand

Callouts can be collapsible, which is handy for details most readers can skip.
:::

title: Quarto features
text:
Tabsets
Tabsets show alternative views of the same thing, one at a time:

SummaryPlotBy cylinders



summary(mtcars$mpg)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   10.40   15.43   19.20   20.09   22.80   33.90




hist(mtcars$mpg, main = NULL, xlab = "Miles per gallon", col = "steelblue")











aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean)
#>   cyl      mpg
#> 1   4 26.66364
#> 2   6 19.74286
#> 3   8 15.10000







Source

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Summary

```{r}
#| label: tabset-summary

summary(mtcars$mpg)
```

## Plot

```{r}
#| label: tabset-plot
#| fig-height: 4

hist(mtcars$mpg, main = NULL, xlab = "Miles per gallon", col = "steelblue")
```

## By cylinders

```{r}
#| label: tabset-by-cyl

aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean)
```
:::

title: Quarto features
text:
Function links
Functions from this package are linked to their reference page, with a tooltip on hover, both inline, like build_site(), and in code:

build_site(devel = TRUE)
preview_site()

In code, functions from other packages are linked to their own documentation, like summary() in the tabset above.

title: Quarto features
text:
Footnotes and margin content
Footnotes are written with [^name].1 Quarto shows them at the end of the page, and as a popup when you hover over the reference.


Source

Footnotes are written with `[^name]`.[^footnote]

[^footnote]: This is a footnote. It can contain *formatting*, `code` and
    [links](https://quarto.org/).

Content can also be placed in the margin.


This note sits in the margin, next to the paragraph it belongs to.

title: Quarto features
text:
Colored output
Output keeps the colors it has in the console, such as cli’s messages and errors:

cli::cli_h2("Checking {.pkg quartodown}")
#> 
#> ── Checking quartodown ──
#> 
cli::cli_alert_success("Found {.val {3}} vignettes.")
#> ✔ Found 3 vignettes.
cli::cli_abort(c(
  "Can't find {.file _quartodown.yml}.",
  "i" = "Create one with {.fn quartodown::use_quartodown}."
))
#> Error:
#> ! Can't find _quartodown.yml.
#> ℹ Create one with `quartodown::use_quartodown()`.

and tibbles:

tibble::tibble(x = c(-1.5, NA, 3), y = c("a", NA, "c"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>       x y    
#>   <dbl> <chr>
#> 1  -1.5 a    
#> 2  NA   NA   
#> 3   3   c

title: Quarto features
text:
Math
Inline math, like \(e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0\), and display math:
\[
  \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
\tag{1}\]
Equations can be referenced too: Equation 1 is the sample mean.


Source

Inline math, like $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$, and display math:

$$
  \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$ {#eq-mean}

Equations can be referenced too: @eq-mean is the sample mean.
